xr-modal.title: WebGL Required
xr-modal.message: AR and VR are not supported on the WebGPU renderer. Pressing OK will reload the viewer with WebGL.
walk-hint.desktop: Click to walk. WASD to move freely.
walk-hint.touch-tap: Tap to walk. Drag to look around.
walk-hint.touch-gaming: Use the joystick to move. Drag to look around. Tap to jump.
artlight.low-precision-picking: This device lacks high-precision picking: measurements use a slower fallback, accurate to a few millimetres.
artlight.point.title: XYZ points
artlight.point.empty: Click or tap the model to place a point.
artlight.point.help: Click a row to copy {axes}. Drag a point to move it, Delete removes the selected point, right-click or Esc clears all.
artlight.coords.height-ellipsoid: H: ellipsoidal height (WGS84), not NGF altitude: about 50 m apart in Provence.
artlight.zero.pick-zero: Click the point of the model to use as zero (Esc to cancel).
artlight.zero.pick-axis: Click a second point: the X axis will pass through it (Esc to cancel).
artlight.zero.axis-vertical: Point is directly above or below the zero: pick another one
artlight.coords.height-ngf-converted: H: NGF-IGN69 altitude, converted from ellipsoidal height with the IGN RAF20 grid (within a few cm).
artlight.coords.height-loading: Loading the NGF grid… H stays ellipsoidal meanwhile.
artlight.coords.height-uncovered: H: ellipsoidal height (WGS84). The scene is outside the NGF-IGN69 grid (mainland France): no conversion.
artlight.coords.height-error: H: ellipsoidal height (WGS84). The NGF grid could not be loaded: no conversion.
artlight.flatness.hint.idle: Click the corners of the area to analyse · Esc to close the tool.
artlight.flatness.hint.more: Click the next corners ({n} more at least).
artlight.flatness.hint.close: Click the first corner or press Enter to close the area.
artlight.flatness.hint.closed: Drag a corner to adjust the area · Esc to clear.
artlight.flatness.title: Flatness
artlight.flatness.banner.lod-loading: loading the finest level of detail…
artlight.flatness.rule-status.no-data: not enough points under the straightedge
artlight.flatness.reference.label: Reference plane
artlight.flatness.reference.mean-title: Flatness: deviations from the plane that best fits the surface
artlight.flatness.reference.horizontal-t: Level: deviations from a horizontal plane at the median height of the area
artlight.flatness.reference.vertical-tit: Plumb: deviations from a vertical plane at the median position of the area
artlight.flatness.reference.only-mean: Best-fit plane: the surface is neither horizontal nor vertical (more than 10° off).
artlight.flatness.info.hatching: Hatching: areas without points, estimated values
artlight.flatness.warn.scale-noise: Scale finer than the survey noise: the map mostly shows noise.
artlight.flatness.lod.finer: finest that could be loaded for this area ({range}, 0 = finest)
artlight.flatness.lod.warn-loading: Provisional measurement on the displayed level of detail: loading the finest level.
artlight.flatness.lod.warn-finer: Area too large for level of detail 0: measured on the finest level that could be loaded. A smaller area will be more accurate.
artlight.flatness.lod.warn-too-large: Area too large to load the finest level of detail: measured on the displayed level. Move closer for more accuracy.
artlight.flatness.lod.warn-failed: Finest level of detail unavailable: measured on the displayed level. Move closer for more accuracy.
artlight.flatness.rule.zone-title: The straightedge spans the area from edge to edge (sagging of a roof slope)
artlight.flatness.rule.no-data: Not enough measured points under the straightedge to conclude.
artlight.flatness.rule.too-small: The area is shorter than the straightedge ({length}) in every direction.
artlight.flatness.rule.too-coarse: Survey not dense enough for this straightedge ({length}): the cloud only allows {cell} cells, at least {n} are needed under the straightedge.
artlight.flatness.rule.trace: White line: least favourable position ({how}, 8 directions, {cell} cells).
artlight.flatness.rule.warn-noise: Tolerance finer than the gap produced by the survey noise (≈ {value}): unreliable verdict.
artlight.flatness.scale.label: Colour scale (±)
artlight.flatness.band.label: Analysed thickness around the best-fit plane
artlight.flatness.band.title: Splats further from the best-fit plane are ignored (objects, roof framing, vegetation…)
artlight.flatness.wave.label: Smooth out tiles
artlight.flatness.wave.title: Removes the undulation of tiles or corrugated sheeting to keep only the shape of the slope. Choose the largest visible dimension of a tile, often its length (30 to 40 cm): the overlaps undulate too.
artlight.flatness.wave.note-zone: To measure the sagging of a slope, choose the "Area" straightedge (Straightedge tab).
artlight.flatness.wave.note-size: Set to the largest visible dimension of a tile (often 30 to 40 cm).
artlight.flatness.hidden.label: Ignore reflections
artlight.flatness.hidden.title: A varnished floor, glossy tiles or a window create ghost splats behind the surface (the reflection). They are discarded: only the layer visible from the viewer is measured.
artlight.flatness.fill.label: Fill gaps
artlight.flatness.export.png-note: Map, legend, scale and results in one image, for a report.
artlight.flatness.export.csv-note: One row per cell: position in the displayed frame and deviation in mm, for Excel.
artlight.flatness.export.copy-note: Results to the clipboard, to paste into Excel or Word.
artlight.flatness.png.title: Flatness — {scene}
artlight.flatness.png.view: Map seen from the viewpoint of the computation. White line: least favourable straightedge position.
artlight.flatness.png.hatching: Hatching: areas without points, estimated values.
artlight.section.title: Section
artlight.section.mode.label: Section type
artlight.section.mode.vertical-title: Vertical section through the clicked point: building section, terrain profile, roof pitch, wall plumb.
artlight.section.mode.horizontal-title: Horizontal section at the height of the clicked point: a plan, seen from above. Click the floor to cut 1 m above it.
artlight.section.mode.points-title: Vertical section between two precise points A and B: road profile, roof pitch between two points.
artlight.section.hint.vertical-idle: Click where to cut. On a wall, the section goes through it · Esc to close the tool.
artlight.section.hint.vertical-done: Click elsewhere to move the section · drag ✥ to shift it, ⟳ to rotate it · Esc to clear.
artlight.section.hint.horizontal-idle: Click the height of the section, or the floor to cut 1 m above it · Esc to close the tool.
artlight.section.hint.horizontal-done: Click elsewhere to change the height · drag ✥ to adjust it · Esc to clear.
artlight.section.hint.points-idle: Click point A, where the section starts · Esc to close the tool.
artlight.section.hint.points-placing: Click point B, where the section ends.
artlight.section.hint.points-done: Drag A or B to move the section · Esc to clear.
artlight.section.failure.too-short: A and B are the same point.
artlight.section.failure.too-short-help: A and B are the same point: place them further apart.
artlight.section.failure.no-data-help: The scene is not loaded yet: wait for loading to finish, then make the section again.
artlight.section.failure.no-points-help: No points in the slice: widen it, or move the section.
artlight.section.orientation.label: Orientation
artlight.section.orientation.title: Angle of the section from North (Y axis in a local frame), measured towards East.
artlight.section.orientation.turn-title: Section perpendicular to the previous one, at the same place.
artlight.section.orientation.face-title: Section parallel to the screen, at the same place.
artlight.section.orientation.plan-title: Rotates the plan view; the section itself does not change.
artlight.section.orientation.walls-title: Section parallel or perpendicular to the wall closest to its current orientation.
artlight.section.orientation.walls-plan-: Rotates the plan view so that walls are straight.
artlight.section.orientation.turn-plan-t: Rotates the plan view by a quarter turn.
artlight.section.orientation.face-plan-t: Plan view oriented like the 3D view.
artlight.section.flip-title: Look at the section from the other side: the hidden side changes, the profile is mirrored.
artlight.section.points.label: Points A and B
artlight.section.swap-note: The profile is then seen from the other side.
artlight.section.thickness.label: Slice thickness
artlight.section.thickness.note: Only points within half this thickness of the section plane are kept. Thinner: a sharper line. Thicker: more points on a sparse cloud.
artlight.section.mask.front: Hide what is in front of the section
artlight.section.mask.above: Hide what is above the section
artlight.section.mask.title: In the 3D view, hides the side the section is seen from, to reveal the cut line.
artlight.section.filter.label: Remove isolated points
artlight.section.filter.title: Removes floating splats, alone in empty space, which clutter the profile.
artlight.section.export.label: Export
artlight.section.export.png-note: Dimensioned profile with graduations, scale, date, project and coordinate system, for a report. The image uses the profile's current framing.
artlight.section.export.dxf-note: For AutoCAD, ArchiCAD…: section points, section lines, dimensions and measurement, in metres, in the displayed coordinate system ({frame}): elevation for a profile, plan position for a horizontal section.
artlight.section.export.csv-note: One row per section point, for Excel: distance, elevation or offset, and coordinates in the displayed system ({frame}).
artlight.section.export.pdf-note: Vector A4 or A3 page for a client or for printing: the section drawn at a standard scale, with title block, results and a 3D view thumbnail. Several sections: "PDF report" in the section folder.
artlight.section.dxf.layer.title: SECTION_TITLE
artlight.section.dxf.axes-profile: X = distance along the section, Y = elevation {axis} ({frame})
artlight.section.dxf.axes-plane: X, Y in the inclined section plane, no real-world coordinates
artlight.section.dxf.points-decimated: {n} of {total} (1 in {step}); the CSV has them all
artlight.section.bar.fit-title: Fit the profile to the whole section
artlight.section.bar.exaggeration-title: Vertical exaggeration: stretches the profile vertically to show small height differences. Dimensions and measurements stay true.
artlight.section.readout.help: Wheel: zoom · drag: pan · click: measure between two points
artlight.section.readout.measure-next: Click the second point of the measurement.
artlight.section.plane.label: Section plane
artlight.section.info.snapped: A and B are snapped to the surface of the cloud.
artlight.section.info.facing: A and B are above one another: the section plane faces the view.
artlight.section.lod.finer: finest loadable for this section ({range}, 0 = finest)
artlight.section.lod.warn-loading: Provisional section on the displayed level of detail: loading the finest one.
artlight.section.lod.warn-finer: Section too large for level of detail 0: it uses the finest level that could be loaded.
artlight.section.lod.warn-too-large: Section too large to load a finer level of detail: it uses the displayed level. Move closer for more precision.
artlight.section.lod.warn-failed: Finest level of detail unavailable: the section uses the displayed level. Move closer for more precision.
artlight.section.png.slice: Points of a {thickness} slice around the section plane ({plane}).
artlight.section.png.exaggeration: Vertical exaggeration ×{n}: heights are stretched, dimensions stay true.
artlight.section.png.no-exaggeration: No exaggeration: same scale for length and height.
artlight.section.png.plan: Top view, oriented at {angle}° from North (Y axis in a local frame).
artlight.section.rule.label: Straightedge and deflection
artlight.section.rule.title: Lays a straightedge on the profile, like a real one on the surface: maximum deflection between two supports, span and L/xxx ratio. Sagging roof or purlin, floor flatness, road depressions.
artlight.section.rule.span-ab-title: The straightedge runs from A to B.
artlight.section.rule.span-pick-title: Click both ends of the straightedge on the profile, on the surface to measure.
artlight.section.rule.pick-first: Straightedge: click its first end on the profile, on the surface to measure.
artlight.section.rule.length-span-title: The straightedge runs from one end of the span to the other: sagging roof, purlin or floor.
artlight.section.rule.length-title: {length} straightedge moved along the span: floor flatness (2 m), road depressions (3 m).
artlight.section.rule.side-above-title: Straightedge laid on the surface: roof, purlin, floor, road. Sagging is always measured from above, even on a rafter seen from inside.
artlight.section.rule.side-below-title: Straightedge held from below: ceiling, slab soffit.
artlight.section.rule.side-left-title: Straightedge on the left of the surface (wall seen edge-on).
artlight.section.rule.side-right-title: Straightedge on the right of the surface (wall seen edge-on).
artlight.section.rule.tiles-title: Wavy surface (tiles, corrugated sheet): the straightedge rests on the tops of the tiles; hollows narrower than the chosen width are filled. Pick the largest visible dimension of a tile, often its length (30 to 40 cm).
artlight.section.rule.tiles-coarse: Survey too sparse to follow the tiles (cells of {cell}): the straightedge rests on the raw surface.
artlight.section.rule.status.too-short: Span too short for this straightedge: place a longer span, or pick a shorter straightedge.
artlight.section.rule.status.too-coarse: Survey too sparse for this straightedge: the point cloud only allows cells of {cell}, at least {n} are needed under the straightedge.
artlight.section.rule.status.no-data: Not enough points under the straightedge: check that the span follows the surface to measure.
artlight.section.rule.how: The straightedge (in blue) rests on the high points of the surface, in cells of {cell}{tiles}. Deflection: largest gap between two supports, perpendicular to the straightedge.
artlight.section.rule.warn-noise: Deflection below the survey noise threshold (≈ {value}): not significant.
artlight.section.png.rule: Straightedge in blue, resting on the high points; deflection measured perpendicular to the straightedge, between two supports.
artlight.section.keep.add-title: Adds the section to the section folder (top right), with its result, its settings and a thumbnail of the 3D view. You can reopen it, rename it and make a report from it.
artlight.section.keep.kept-title: This section is in the folder as “{name}”.
artlight.section.keep.update-title: Replaces “{name}” in the folder with the section as it is now.
artlight.section.keep.copy-title: Adds the section to the folder as a new section; “{name}” stays as it was.
artlight.section.keep.wait-loading: Wait until the finest level of detail has loaded.
artlight.section.folder.title: Section folder
artlight.section.folder.open-title: Reopen “{name}” to view or edit it
artlight.section.folder.note: Sections stay in the folder while the page is open.
artlight.section.folder.report-title: A vector PDF: cover page and contents, then one page per section, in folder order.
artlight.section.pdf.intro-section: The open section on one page, drawn to scale, with its title block, results and a 3D view thumbnail.
artlight.section.pdf.intro-folder: A cover page with the contents, then the folder sections ({n}) in list order, one per page.
artlight.section.pdf.fallback: "{name}" does not fit on the page at {forced}: it is drawn at {scale}.
artlight.section.pdf.cover-note: Sections extracted from the 3D survey (point cloud). Dimensions and elevations in metres, in the stated coordinate system. The scale is declared in the PDF: Acrobat's measuring tool reads metres.
artlight.section.pdf.creator: Artlight viewer
artlight.section.pdf.dialog.scale-auto-t: For each section, the largest standard scale (1:20, 1:50, 1:100…) that fits on the page.
artlight.section.pdf.dialog.scale-forced: All sections at {scale}. A section too large for the page gets the automatic scale.
artlight.section.pdf.dialog.lines-only-t: Cleaner drawing: section lines, dimensions and measurements, without the slice point cloud.
artlight.section.pdf.dialog.failed: The PDF could not be created: {error}
artlight.map.title: Map
artlight.map.goto-hint: Click to go there; scroll, drag or pinch to zoom and move the map
artlight.map.marks-hint: Show or hide annotations, portals, starting view and room names
artlight.speed.label: Movement speed
artlight.quality.label: Display quality
artlight.quality.help-auto: Best quality your device can display smoothly.
artlight.quality.help-standard: Lighter image, smoother on modest devices.
artlight.quality.help-medium: Full resolution, less detail than High: faster to load.
artlight.quality.help-high: Full resolution and more detail, even if the display slows down.
artlight.quality.hint-reduced: Display too slow: switched to standard quality (HD menu to change)
